source: twelve relations of the second confirmatory batch, specified from publisher documentation (e3/truth/docs/fresh2/) by three subagents that never saw data, mined FDs or model answers; parts A (benchmarks), B (ChEMBL, MusicBrainz, PLUTO, FHRS), C (GeoNames, EIA-860, STATS19, GHCN)
rule: part A: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, unique constraint, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. For the three BenchBase benchmarks the DDL at the pinned commit is the specification of the generated data (scale factor 1); a dependency that the H-Store project page states and the DDL neither declares nor contradicts is ambiguous and is recorded with sure: false, quoting both. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened. | part B: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, unique constraint on a NOT NULL column, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one or containment statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out, when two documents conflict, or when a unique index covers a nullable column. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state, and documented non-dependencies, are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened. | part C: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one or nesting statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened.

instance.generator: public data fixed before download for the second confirmatory evaluation, converted by unpack_fresh2.py and joined by fresh.py
instance.construction: EIA-860 final 2025 data, eia8602025.zip ('Release Date: September 10, 2026, Final 2025 data'): the Operable sheet of 3_1_Generator_Y2025.xlsx (root; 'those generators which are currently operating, out of service or on standby') left-joined to the Plant sheet of 2___Plant_Y2025.xlsx on Plant Code and to the Utility sheet of 1___Utility_Y2025.xlsx on Utility ID (sheet names confirmed from the workbooks; the unpack exports each sheet with its header unchanged as eia/<workbook>__<sheet>.csv), the columns being the Field Names of the Field Directory of LayoutY2025.xlsx; dropped the generator file's Utility ID, Utility Name, Plant Name, State and County copies, Technology, Duct Burners, the heat recovery, RTO/ISO, DC Net Capacity, uprate/derate, operating, retirement and planned-retirement items, Energy Source 3-6, Startup Source 1-4, the combined-heat, gasification, carbon-capture, combustion-technology, turbine, wind and solar items; the plant file's Street Address, City, State, Zip, County, Balancing Authority Name, Name of Water Source (free text), Regulatory Status, Sector, Sector Name, the FERC docket numbers, ash-impoundment, transmission-owner, grid-voltage, energy-storage and natural-gas items; the utility file's Street Address, City, State, Zip and the four relationship flags.

truth.clause: eia860_instructions.pdf, SCHEDULE 3. GENERATOR INFORMATION, item 7, p. 9: "Each generator must be uniquely identified within a plant."; eia860_instructions.pdf, SCHEDULE 3. PART A, line 1, p. 9: "Generator identification should be the same identification as reported on other EIA forms to be uniquely defined within a plant."; eia860_page.html: "3_1_GeneratorYyyyy — Contains generator-level data for the surveyed generators, split into three tabs."; eia_LayoutY2025__Field_Directory.csv, row 55: Field Name "Generator ID", Description "Generator identification number"; row 59: "Ownership", "Identifies the ownership for each generator"; row 66: "Summer Capacity (MW)", "The net summer capacity"; row 67: "Winter Capacity (MW)", "The net winter capacity"; row 88: "Energy Source 1", "The code representing the most predominant type of energy that fuels the generator"; row 89: "Energy Source 2", "The code representing the second most predominant type of energy that fuels the generator"
truth.justification: The generator ID is unique within a plant, so the pair (Plant Code, Generator ID) identifies one generator, whose Schedule 3 items (prime mover, unit code, ownership, capacities, power factor, minimum load, status, energy sources) are reported once per generator in the generator-level file; the Field Directory rows give the published names of the Schedule 3 items (ownership code, net summer and winter capacity, predominant and second energy source).

truth.justification: The EIA Plant Code is EIA's identifier of a plant and Schedule 2 is answered once per plant (name, coordinates, NERC region, balancing authority, NAICS code, FERC statuses on lines 1-11), published in the plant-level file; a plant connected to more than one balancing authority still selects one on line 5 ('If you believe the plant is connected to more than one balancing authority, explain in SCHEDULE 7'); the Field Directory rows give the published names of the line 5 code and the line 8 NAICS code.
